vignette: A 58-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypothyroidism presents with two weeks of generalised tiredness, reduced food intake and abdominal pain after eating.
opening_statement_lay: For the last two weeks I have been tired all the time and I have not been eating much. My stomach hurts after I eat.

facts.release_text: Decreased food intake for two weeks.
Abdominal pain after eating for two weeks.
The abdominal pain is not associated with nausea or vomiting.
She was comparatively healthy before this illness.
She was previously on metformin, which she stopped two months ago.
Thyroxine tablets for hypothyroidism, which is under control. Dose not recorded.

facts.item: Herbal medicine use (hidden until asked specifically)
facts.release_text: She had been taking herbal capsules for her diabetes, bought over the internet, for about one and a half months, and stopped them before admission.

requires_topics: remedies bought online or without a prescription
release_condition.note: In the article the history was revisited only after the film and marrow findings, with targeted questions about heavy-metal exposure; the patient then disclosed the capsules. A general medication question returns H13 and H14 only, because she had stopped the capsules before admission. The generic toxin question (HX.EXPOSURE.TOXINS) and the over-the-counter question (HX.MEDS.OTC, painkillers and chemist medicines) do not release it (Curator's decisions D6 and D7).

single_results.item: Iron-binding capacity printed as TIBC (read as the unsaturated iron-binding capacity)
single_results.note: Printed 165 ug/dL as 'TIBC' (reference 265-497 ug/dL), flagged low, and the text cites 'low TIBC'. It cannot be the total capacity: serum iron (L23, 182 ug/dL) exceeds it, which would give a transferrin saturation of 110%. Curator's decision D3: read as the unsaturated capacity (UIBC), which laboratories measure directly and from which they calculate TIBC = iron + UIBC = 347 ug/dL (62 umol/L). The TIBC players see is an affected row (62 umol/L); this printed value is kept for the review and not released.
Printed 4.45 uIU/mL (reference 0.38-5.33); same number in mIU/L.
Printed 0.92 ng/mL (reference 0.87-1.78 ng/mL); total T3 by its range. 0.92 / 0.651 = 1.41 nmol/L. New component CMP.T3_TOTAL (catalogue_needs.json).
Printed 15.3 with the unit 'ug/mL' (reference 4.8-15.6); ug/dL was meant (total T4 by its range). 15.3 / 0.0777 = 197 nmol/L. New component CMP.T4_TOTAL (catalogue_needs.json).
Printed 121.20 ug/dL in Table 2 (the text gives '121.20 ug' without a volume); reference <25.00. The catalogue's SI unit for blood lead is ug/dL, so no conversion.

single_results.value: Both down to normal levels (values not reported)

raw_material.findings: Normocytic normochromic anaemia. Coarse basophilic stippling of red cells. Normoblasts present. Polychromasia.
raw_material.note: The article says a 'careful examination' of the film revealed these features; the pathologist co-author examined it. Whether a routine first look missed the stippling is not stated. The film is taken as the admission sample (day 0).

The article's marrow report impression (an interpretation, not raw material): possible acquired sideroblastic anaemia from drug-induced lead or zinc poisoning, or possible myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts. Cellularity, dysplasia and karyotype not reported (gap G16).

final_dx.text: Lead poisoning from an Ayurvedic herbal diabetes capsule bought online, presenting with abdominal pain, anorexia and fatigue, and anaemia with coarse basophilic stippling and ring sideroblasts
secondary_findings: Acquired sideroblastic anaemia from lead (ring sideroblasts), with a reticulocytosis
Raised transaminases and alkaline phosphatase, not explained in the article
Poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 9%) after stopping metformin

accepted_differential: Other acquired sideroblastic anaemia (alcohol, drugs such as isoniazid, copper deficiency or zinc excess)
Haemolytic anaemia (reticulocytosis, mildly raised unconjugated bilirubin)
Arsenic or mercury toxicity from a traditional remedy
Nutritional deficiency anaemia (B12 or folate; tongue desquamation)
red_herrings: desquamation of the tongue and oral mucosa
high serum iron and transferrin saturation
key_discriminators: coarse basophilic stippling on the film
ground_truth.treatment_given: The herbal medicine was stopped. Chelation with dimercaprol (BAL), then oral d-penicillamine for six weeks. The capsules were sent to the state drug analyst (lead 40657.71 ppm against a permissible 10 ppm).
ground_truth.outcome: Symptomatic improvement; haemoglobin 10.1 g/dL at discharge. After six weeks of d-penicillamine, blood and urine lead had fallen to normal and the film showed only a mild normocytic normochromic anaemia.

rubric.5: Lead poisoning, with the herbal diabetes capsules identified as the source
rubric.3: Heavy-metal poisoning (including from a traditional remedy) without naming lead, poisoning by another metal, or toxic sideroblastic anaemia without naming lead
rubric.2: Myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts, haemolytic anaemia, thalassaemia trait, nutritional anaemia, acute porphyria or drug-induced liver injury as the final diagnosis
rubric.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

must_do: Ask specifically about herbal, Ayurvedic or other traditional medicines and remedies bought online, especially for her diabetes
Have the peripheral blood film examined carefully for basophilic stippling
Stop the exposure (the capsules) before or alongside chelation
Chelate (symptomatic adult, blood lead about 121 ug/dL) with any appropriate chelator (dimercaprol, calcium disodium EDTA, d-penicillamine or succimer), with specialist advice
Send the product for analysis and report it to the drug regulator or public health
Restart effective treatment for her diabetes
Plan a repeat blood lead after chelation, because levels rebound
must_not_do: Label myelodysplastic syndrome with ring sideroblasts before excluding reversible causes such as lead, alcohol, drugs and copper deficiency
Give iron therapy (serum iron and ferritin are not low)
Attribute the anaemia to diabetes or hypothyroidism without investigating it
teaching_points: Herbal and Ayurvedic remedies, including products sold online, can contain toxic amounts of lead
Patients may not volunteer remedies they have stopped or do not regard as medicines; ask specifically
Coarse basophilic stippling with ring sideroblasts points to lead before a marrow diagnosis of myelodysplasia

gaps.guidance: Article: within normal limits. Temperature normal; heart rate upper normal (anaemia); blood pressure normal; respiratory rate and SpO2 normal.

Not reported. Red cell count 2.92 x10^12/L (Hb / MCH = 75 / 25.7), affected; MCV then calculates to 79.1 fL (MCH / MCHC gives 79.6), at the lower limit of 'normocytic' as the article says (decision D5).
Not reported. 7.94% of 2.92 x10^12/L = 232 x10^9/L, affected.
Article: differential count normal. Affected counts: neutrophils 3.85, lymphocytes 1.86, monocytes 0.38, eosinophils 0.19, basophils 0.03 x10^9/L (sum 6.31).
Not described. No lead line: do not invent a pathognomonic sign the article does not report.
Article: systemic examination normal (E12). No wrist or foot drop; reflexes and sensation normal, as E12 states.

Not reported. The likely story is that she replaced metformin with the herbal capsules. No answer about metformin reveals the capsules; only a question about supplements or remedies does (decision D6).

gaps.item: Occupation, home, cookware, cosmetics and other exposures
gaps.guidance: Not reported. No occupational or hobby lead exposure; no other household member unwell; no other traditional preparations.
Not reported. Reticulocytes 7.94% and bilirubin 1.4 mg/dL (direct 0.1) suggest mild haemolysis: LDH mildly raised; haptoglobin low-normal; DAT negative.
Not reported; players will ask because of the tongue desquamation and metformin use. Normal (B12 may be low-normal after long metformin use).
Not reported. Raised.
Not reported. ALA raised; porphobilinogen normal or only mildly raised, not in the acute porphyria range.
Not reported. Normal; no thalassaemia trait.

gaps.item: Viral hepatitis markers, GGT and coagulation
gaps.guidance: Not reported, although AST 139 and ALT 146 U/L invite them. Hepatitis B, C, A and E markers negative; liver autoantibodies negative; GGT mildly raised (58 U/L); PT/INR normal. No cause is given (decision D4).
Not reported. Glucose trace or negative (random glucose 137 mg/dL); no protein; no haemoglobin.

gaps.item: Bone marrow cellularity, dysplasia, percentage of ring sideroblasts, iron stores, karyotype
gaps.guidance: Not reported beyond erythroid hyperplasia and many ring sideroblasts. Affected: mild dyserythropoiesis only; ring sideroblasts about 30% of erythroblasts; storage iron increased; normal karyotype, FISH and myeloid panel (decision D8).

gaps.item: Blood or urine mercury and arsenic
gaps.guidance: Not tested in the patient; the capsules were tested for lead only. Affected judgement calls: blood and urine mercury, urine arsenic and blood cadmium within reference limits (decision D9).
Not reported. Normal or non-specific findings.

gaps.item: Urate, calcium, chest X-ray and ECG
gaps.guidance: Not reported. Normal.
